items.claim: The boundary rationale rests entirely on a Hebrew lexical-homograph claim (a positive covenant-kindness sense vs. a rarer reproach sense sharing one spelling) but never quotes the Hebrew word or cites its MT verse.
items.evidence: Prov.14.34's B-colon noun is spelled וְחֶ֖סֶד (byte tier, per verse_map_oshb.json) -- the same pointed form standardly used for the positive sense elsewhere -- but the rationale and observed_substrate_signals describe the homograph entirely in English, quoting no Hebrew run, and boundary_evidence_refs cites only the parent-collection span (web:Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16), with no oshb: citation for the verse itself. Independent check: WEB's own rendering ('sin is a disgrace to any people') does track the rarer sense argued for, so the underlying claim is not contested by the bytes -- only the citation/quotation is missing, which the lens treats as insufficient engagement for a Hebrew-dependent claim.
tier_citations: oshb:Prov.14.34 (byte, verified independently, not quoted by the row)

items.claim: The verse's two negated clauses restate one resistance-to-correction rather than opposing two subjects, and the scoffer term does not recur in the immediate vicinity, matching the synthetic-parallelism call.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.15.12 byte text לֹ֣א יֶאֱהַב לֵ֭ץ הוֹכֵ֣חַֽ ל֑וֹ אֶל חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים לֹ֣א יֵלֵֽךְ shows both cola opening their negation with the same particle (twice), no adversative marker, matching WEB's semicolon (not 'but') rendering. Skeleton sweep of לץ (scoffer) returns 14 book-wide verse hits with nearest neighbors at Prov.14.6 and Prov.19.25 -- no recurrence between them, confirming the 'does not recur elsewhere in this part' signal.
tier_citations: skeleton sweep לץ: 14 verses book-wide, none between 14.6 and 19.25 besides 15.12

items.claim: The observed signal that face/spirit imagery is not repeated in the surrounding verses is byte-false: the immediately following verse carries an undisclosed inline occurrence of the same root at the row's own seam.
items.evidence: Skeleton sweep of פני returns 48 book-wide verse hits including the consecutive pair Prov.15.13 (פָּנִ֑ים, byte) and Prov.15.14, whose raw oshb text carries an unpointed inline token ופני between דָּ֑עַת and the pointed וּפִ֥י -- the same face/panim root touching the row's own seam. This is an undisclosed cross-seam recurrence (a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed); the antithetic reading of Prov.15.13 on its own terms is not overturned, since the governing qere sense at 15:14 is 'mouth' not 'face,' but the 'not repeated' claim as written needs correction/disclosure.
tier_citations: skeleton sweep פני: 48 verses book-wide incl. consecutive 15.13/15.14

items.claim: The ketiv/qere identification is inverted and misattributed: the fully-pointed ordinary word for 'knowledge' is labeled the inline ketiv token, and the actual unpointed ketiv is labeled 'the qere,' while the true qere word is never named.
items.evidence: The raw oshb:Prov.15.14 byte string sequence is: ... דָּ֑עַת ופני וּפִ֥י ...: דָּ֑עַת is fully pointed and unrelated to the K/Q note (it is simply the object of 'seeks' in the A-colon); the unpointed inline token immediately after it, ופני, is the actual ketiv (matching the toolkit's own INLINE-KETIV HAZARD pattern -- an unpointed ketiv token inline before the pointed qere), and the true qere is the following pointed word וּפִ֥י ('mouth'), which the row never names. pmarks_Prov.json confirms one K/Q note at Prov.15.14 (kq count=1, count-only -- word identity is not sourceable from the inventory itself, only from the verse bytes), and the byte evidence does not support the row's word assignment. The verse's own antithetic wise-heart/fool-mouth reading is unaffected, but the K/Q disclosure as written is byte-false.

items.claim: The verse pairs a temporal totalizer with a non-comparative 'good of heart' predicate, correctly lacking the tov-min construction that binds the following pair.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.15.15 byte text כָּל יְמֵ֣י עָנִ֣י רָעִ֑ים וְטֽוֹב לֵ֝֗ב מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד opens on the 'all the days' totalizer and carries the טוב word mid-verse as a construct ('good of heart') with no comparative marker prefixed to a following noun, unlike the verse-initial טוב-plus-comparative construction confirmed at Prov.15.16-17.

items.claim: Both quoted closing tags collate at byte tier to their cited verses, and the verse-initial tov-comparative construction is confirmed unique to this consecutive pair in the surrounding chapter.
items.evidence: collate.py --json confirms tier=byte for the closing two-word tag of Prov.15.16 against oshb:Prov.15.16 and the closing two-word tag of Prov.15.17 against oshb:Prov.15.17 (both quotes spliced programmatically from verse_map_oshb.json, not hand-typed). Skeleton sweep of טוב returns 63 verses book-wide; checking first-token position across Prov.15.15-15.20 shows only 15.16 and 15.17 open verse-initial with טוב, each followed by a comparative-marked target word (מֵאוֹצָ֥ר / מִשּׁ֥וֹר), matching the construction-run claim.
tier_citations: skeleton sweep טוב: 63 verses book-wide, verse-initial only at 15.16/15.17 in the local span

items.claim: The ma'aneh root genuinely recurs at the two non-adjacent verses named, and the rejected pairing with the preceding verse correctly finds no shared token.
items.evidence: oshb byte forms confirm the ma'aneh-root opener of Prov.15.1 (מַֽעֲנֶה רַּ֭ךְ יָשִׁ֣יב חֵמָ֑ה וּדְבַר עֶ֝֗צֶב יַעֲלֶה אָֽף), the ma'aneh-root construct of Prov.15.23 (שִׂמְחָ֣ה לָ֭אִישׁ בְּמַעֲנֵה פִ֑יו וְדָבָ֖ר בְּעִתּ֣וֹ מַה טּֽוֹב), and the ma'aneh-root closer of Prov.16.1 (לְאָדָ֥ם מַֽעַרְכֵי לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מַעֲנֵ֥ה לָשֽׁוֹן), all forms of the same root, non-adjacent to one another as claimed. Lexical comparison of Prov.15.22 (הָפֵ֣ר מַ֭חֲשָׁבוֹת בְּאֵ֣ין ס֑וֹד וּבְרֹ֖ב יוֹעֲצִ֣ים תָּקֽוּם) against Prov.15.23 shows no shared root, supporting the rejected-alternative claim.

items.claim: The antithetic verb pair is byte-confirmed, and the disclosed paseq mark is correctly sourced from the inventory as a single-witness corroboration rather than a boundary driver.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.15.25 byte text בֵּ֣ית גֵּ֭אִים יִסַּ֥ח יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝יַצֵּ֗ב גְּב֣וּל אַלְמָנָֽה confirms the tear-down/set-firm verb opposition. pmarks_Prov.json confirms one paseq seg at Prov.15.25 (count-only, per its own paseq_note 'citable from this inventory only'), matching the row's '(single-witness)' disclosure. Lexical comparison against Prov.15.26 (תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת רָ֑ע וּ֝טְהֹרִ֗ים אִמְרֵי נֹֽעַם) confirms only the divine name is shared and no other point of contact exists.
